reason: The cited evidence supports that high entropy can stabilize solid solutions at high temperatures (E1, E2) and that lattice distortion exists (E4), but no cited passage provides specific evidence that lattice distortion impedes diffusion-driven ordering or that this balance governs stability up to 1923 K in nanoparticles; the mechanistic link between distortion and suppressed diffusion is asserted without direct support.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a random solid solution at elevated temperatures
Severe lattice distortion from atomic size mismatches impedes diffusion-driven ordering
Entropy and lattice distortion effects can remain dominant over the enthalpic drive for chemical segregation
